novelty.summary: The full Hafezi-Reiss paper and relevant sections of the peer-reviewed equalization review were read. The update narrows masking claims, separates magnitude from phase topology and records that the current EQNormalizer is single-track static spectral correction rather than the cited cross-adaptive multitrack algorithm.

source_cards.title: Autonomous Multitrack Equalization Based on Masking Reduction
source_cards.bounded_summary: A cross-adaptive K-by-K track comparison identifies frequencies where a louder masker is nonessential and a maskee is essential, then applies bounded or unbounded peaking cuts. The controller is an engineering-inspired heuristic rather than a calibrated auditory model. Objective MUR changes were small and did not consistently predict subjective masking or preference.

methods.offline: non-overlapping 1024-point FFT average over full excerpt; up to three second-order IIR peaking cuts per track
methods.realtime: ten octave-band RMS filters, EMA smoothing, up to five time-varying peaking filters per track
methods.analysis_channel: stereo tracks converted to mono for detection

source_numeric_settings_not_project_pres.origin: paper implementation; several values selected by informal listening

limitations: The controller omits masking caused by a quieter masker that still raises audibility threshold.
Several filter and ranking parameters were chosen by informal listening.
MUR improvements were small and sometimes negative by song.
Objective masking reduction did not consistently predict subjective masking or preference.
The no-reference multistimulus test forced use of scale extremes and may exaggerate differences.
Only nine participant results remained after exclusion and playback used one headphone setup.
No source-code reproduction was completed in this run.

source_cards.title: All About Audio Equalization: Solutions and Frontiers
source_cards.bounded_summary: The review separates minimum-phase, linear-phase, dynamic, targeted and noise/masking equalizers. Linear phase trades phase response for latency and possible pre-ringing; dynamic EQ requires explicit detector ballistics; real-time target matching benefits from activity gating and response smoothing.
limitations: This is a broad review, not a rock-mix listening study.
The Hafezi-Reiss summary is secondary evidence and describes results as mixed.
The linked code repository timed out, so reproducibility verification is partial.

implementation_audit_cards.observed_behavior: single-input static spectral-profile correction using averaged magnitude, fixed hand-authored target curves and fixed-center EQ band fitting
not_observed: essential versus nonessential frequency ranking across tracks
filter realization, phase response or latency verification
implementation_audit_cards.test_scope: unit tests cover shapes, fallbacks, gain clamp and OSC serialization; they do not test source equivalence, target provenance, silence behavior, phase, listening preference or full-mix masking
implementation_audit_cards.bounded_conclusion: The module may be a valid independent static correction component, but the Hafezi citation is contextual and must not be treated as proof that the paper's cross-adaptive method or results were implemented.

knowledge_cards.title: Masking proxy is not masking ground truth
knowledge_cards.claim: The Hafezi-Reiss controller is an engineering heuristic and its MUR evaluator showed weak, inconsistent alignment with musical preference; neither should be used as a sole masking label.

knowledge_cards.title: Cross-adaptive evidence requires cross-track implementation
knowledge_cards.claim: Results from a K-by-K masker-maskee system do not validate a single-track target-spectrum normalizer.

knowledge_cards.title: More objective de-masking need not mean better mix
knowledge_cards.claim: Masking score, source distinguishability and overall preference must be reported separately.

knowledge_cards.title: Magnitude match does not choose phase topology
knowledge_cards.claim: Minimum-phase IIR, linear-phase FIR and zero-phase offline realizations can share a magnitude target while differing in latency, phase and transient artifacts.

knowledge_cards.title: Linear phase is not automatically transparent
knowledge_cards.claim: Linear-phase EQ can avoid phase distortion yet add latency and pre-ringing; it requires transient and workflow checks rather than a quality label.

knowledge_cards.title: Adaptive targets need activity gating and smoothing
knowledge_cards.claim: A time-varying target system should exclude inactive/noisy frames and smooth desired and applied responses before it can be evaluated musically.

knowledge_cards.title: Dynamic EQ requires explicit control law
knowledge_cards.claim: Dynamic EQ conclusions are incomplete without threshold/detector, attack, release, band, range, topology and gain-trace context.

knowledge_cards.title: Citation is not implementation validation
knowledge_cards.claim: A paper cited in a module docstring must be traced to implemented analysis, controls and tests before its evidence is inherited.

revisions_to_existing_conclusions.previous: Spectral similarity is not psychoacoustic masking.
revisions_to_existing_conclusions.revised: Correct and retained. Hafezi-Reiss also does not provide ground-truth masking: its controller omits an explicit auditory model and its MUR evaluator aligned weakly with musical judgments.

revisions_to_existing_conclusions.previous: Static versus dynamic action follows persistence.
revisions_to_existing_conclusions.revised: Retain only as engineering inference. Literature supports explicit time variation, activity gating and smoothing, but does not prove that every intermittent collision should receive dynamic EQ.
revisions_to_existing_conclusions.reason: avoid converting topology description into a prescriptive rule

revisions_to_existing_conclusions.previous: Existing active advisory rule cites jaes_hafezi_reiss_masking_eq and carries project gain/Q bounds.
revisions_to_existing_conclusions.revised: The paper supports prioritizing high-valued detected events within its own heuristic, but does not validate the current project bounds or a different single-track normalizer. Keep active rule unchanged in this research run; schedule source-to-rule audit before future promotion.

rule_candidates.title: Name the spectral process correctly
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: A component or card claims masking reduction from spectral analysis.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Label single-track target matching, cross-track overlap and cross-adaptive masking as separate methods; expose inputs and controller graph.
rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Map every cited method block to implemented inputs, state, parameters and tests.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: The implementation cannot reproduce the cited analysis graph or the label overstates the evidence.

rule_candidates.title: Keep masking, clarity and preference separate
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Report controller score, independent masking/clarity judgment and overall preference as separate outcomes.
rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Blind loudness-matched ratings plus score traces and full-mix comments.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: Only the optimized metric improves or listener preference falls.

rule_candidates.title: Constrain cross-adaptive attenuation experimentally
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: A cross-track collision persists after role-aware level and pan baselines.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Test a project attenuation grid of 0/1/2/3 dB with identical detector and topology; do not import the paper's 6 dB cap or Q values as defaults.
rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Gain trace, full mix, mono and blind loudness-matched preference.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: A lower bound performs as well, action is audible outside collisions, or preference declines.

rule_candidates.title: Gate inactive frames before adaptive target estimation
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: A target or correction is estimated continuously from changing input.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Exclude silence and low-level noise with a calibrated activity decision before updating the target estimate.

proposed_range.origin: must be calibrated on project recordings

rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Label active/inactive frames and inspect false closure, target jitter and noise pumping.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: Quiet intentional content is excluded or the gate creates discontinuity.

rule_candidates.title: Smooth adaptive target and applied filter separately
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: EQ parameters change frame by frame.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Log and tune target-response smoothing and applied-filter smoothing as separate controls.

proposed_range.origin: must be derived from one-factor experiments

rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Parameter-jitter metrics, step response and blind full-song listening.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: The correction chatters, lags musical changes or pumps between events.

rule_candidates.title: Separate magnitude target from EQ phase topology
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: A target curve can be realized by minimum-phase, linear-phase or zero-phase processing.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Hold the magnitude target fixed and compare topology as an independent factor.
rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Measure magnitude, impulse response, group delay, latency and pre-ringing; then blind loudness-matched A/B.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: Magnitude differs materially, latency exceeds use case or transient artifacts outweigh benefit.

rule_candidates.title: Require behavior-level tests before inheriting paper evidence
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: A DSP/ML module cites a research method.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Add tests for the cited method's defining behavior before claiming equivalence; structural unit tests are insufficient.
rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Synthetic fixtures and licensed-audio evaluation that isolate each defining behavior.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: The component is intentionally a different method; then revise provenance language instead of forcing equivalence.

handoff: Treat EQNormalizer as single-track static spectral-profile correction, not validated cross-adaptive de-masking. Keep unchanged and level/pan baselines. For any time-varying EQ candidate, expose detector, activity gate, smoothing, filter topology and gain trace; judge masking, target fit and preference separately in a loudness-matched full-mix and mono test.
